learning_outcomes.text: Explain the operating principles of thermal systems and the interactions between their components.
Describe the thermodynamic processes and transfer phenomena necessary for the design of thermal installations.
Identify dimensioning criteria for heat exchangers, pipes, tanks, and auxiliary equipment.
Explain energetic and exergetic analysis methods applied to thermal systems.
Describe procedures for evaluating performance, efficiency, and operational safety.
Model and dimension thermal components using analytical relationships and digital tools.
Utilize dedicated software for heat transfer analysis, fluid flow, and thermal simulations.
Develop operating diagrams and technological schemes for thermal systems.
Analyze the performance and dynamic behavior of designed systems.
Propose constructive solutions and measures for energetic optimization.
Respect professional and safety standards in the design of thermal systems.
Collaborate efficiently in multidisciplinary teams in design activities.
Manage information resources and software tools autonomously.
Develop complete and well-argued technical documentation for the projects carried out.

syllabus_topics: Thermal systems and their role in industry
Fundamental thermodynamic processes applied in design
General structure of a thermal system
Design of thermal networks and pipes
Combustion systems and thermal energy generation
Energetic and exergetic analysis of thermal systems
Analysis of a simple thermal system: Operating schemes and elementary balances
Determination of thermal parameters of materials: Conductivity, thermal resistance, use of measuring instruments
Dimensioning of a heat exchanger: Thermal and hydraulic calculation, verifications and correlations
Simulation of heat transfer using specialized software: Numerical analyses in steady and transient regimes
Hydraulic calculation of a pipe network: Pressure losses, flow regimes
Exergetic analysis of a thermal system: Determination of losses and exergetic efficiency
Practical design study of a complete thermal system: Integration of calculations; technical synthesis and final discussion
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures with visual presentations, graphics, schemes, and illustrative models of thermal systems
Explanation of theoretical concepts accompanied by discussions, guided questions, and practical examples
Discovery-based learning through numerical tests, analytical modeling, equipment demonstrations, or digital simulations
Correlation of theoretical notions with case analyses and practical design problems
Laboratory activities complement theoretical teaching through applied exercises, computer-assisted simulations, and work with technical models
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 10 to 1 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the awarding of corresponding study credits.
